newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy Jan new car sales seen up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy Jan new car sales seen up 10 pct.

text.p: Italy's car market looks like starting 1997 on a firm footing with new car registrations in January seen up around 10 percent on January last year, industrial sources and analysts said.
"There should be a rise in registrations of at least 10 percent to some 220,000 units," one sector source said.

The government's cash incentive scheme introduced in January to encourage motorists to trade in cars over 10 years old for scrap in exchange for buying a new car "gave the market a boost in the second half of January," the source said.
New car registrations in December stood at 111,000, a jump of 12.14 percent year-on-year.

Analysts noted January is normally a good month for the Italian car market, benefiting from purchases already decided on in the final part of the previous year but delayed until the New Year, above all for tax reasons.
"Usually the year starts off with around 200,000 registrations. In January last year there were 198,600," one industry source said.

Fiat group marques, dominating nearly half the domestic market, should see a healthy rise. "The incentive scheme will especially benefit the small to medium size model range and so Fiat will certainly see higher sales," the source said.

Fiat Auto has said January orders from Italian dealers were up by 35 to 40 percent year-on-year. The Turin-based carmaker had earlier forecast an increase in sales of up to 250,000 in the nine-month period the incentive scheme will operate.

But even top of the range marques were seen posting higher sales. Mercedes saw January sales up 18.6 percent to 3,300 units. "And this growth could have been even higher if we had had more cars to deliver," a Mercedes spokesman said.
Analysts said the impact of increased orders on new registrations data would be apparent above all in February and March when the new cars will have been delivered.

"I see a rise in January registrations of 7-8 percent to just under 220,000," said Giampaolo Trasi, analyst at Milan brokers IMI-Sigeco. "Without the incentive scheme the car market in January would have been a carbon copy of 1996. We see the scheme increasing sales by some 150,000 over the next nine months," he said.

"It is too soon for registrations in January to show the full impact of the scheme because many ordered cars have not yet been delivered. But the effects will be much stronger in February and March," Trasi added.
